chunks: And through it, from Abban bin Taghlub, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said:

What will you be like when the 'Sabtah' occurs between the two mosques, at which knowledge will be bound in it as a snake binds in its hole, and the Shia will disagree among themselves, and some will call others liars, and some will spit in the faces of others?
So I said: 'What goodness is there in that?'
He said: 'All the goodness is in that.' He said it three times, meaning that deliverance would be near.

key_terms.السَّبْطَةُ: The Sabtah, a period of concealment or testing for the Shia, often associated with the time between the two mosques.
key_terms.الْخَيْرُ: Goodness or benefit, which the Imam asserts is present even in the midst of turmoil.
key_terms.الْفَرَجِ: Deliverance or relief, referring to the appearance of the Mahdi (as) and the end of the occultation.
key_terms.يَأْرَزَ: To bind or coil tightly, used here metaphorically for knowledge being concentrated yet confined.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Sabtah and the state of knowledge during it according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the 'Sabtah' as a critical era of eschatological testing where scholarly authority becomes concentrated yet fragmented, leading to intense internal strife and mutual excommunication among the Shia. Imam al-Sadiq (as) underscores that despite this turmoil, the period is inherently blessed because it marks the imminent arrival of the Mahdi’s reappearance (al-Faraj), a theme deeply rooted in Shia eschatological tradition.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (7) Abban bin Taghlub narrated that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “What will you do if a time comes to you between the two mosques, at which knowledge will be bound as a snake bound in its hole and the Shia will disagree among themselves, will call each other as liars and will spit at the face of each other?”
Abban said: “What goodness will be in that?” He said: “All the goodness will be in that.”

He said it three times and he meant that deliverance would be near.” The same was narrated by Muhammad bin Ya’qoob al-Kulayni from some of his companions from Ahmad bin Muhammad from al-Hasan bin Ali al-Washsha’ from Ali bin al-Husayn from Abban bin Taghlub from Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as).
